items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 24 at 2:14PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:

Tuesday morning and will continue through Tuesday evening before
diminishing Tuesday night. The strongest winds are expected
between 8 AM and 6 PM Tuesday. Periods of rain will accompany the
strong winds through much of the day.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 24 at 2:12PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Water levels are currently rising and will peak around 2 to 3
feet above the normal high tide line with the Monday evening and
Tuesday afternoon high tides. Highest levels are expected from
Point Hope to Wainwright. Water levels gradually return to near
normal levels Tuesday night.
items.areas: Western Arctic Coast; Northwest Arctic Coast; Northern Arctic Coast

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 24 at 1:34PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Areas of rain on Tuesday will transition to snow in the Eastern
Brooks Range Tuesday evening. Snow then continues through the day
on Wednesday. Given the rain beforehand, snow will struggle to
accumulate immediately but there will be minor accumulations by
Wednesday morning. Wednesday afternoon there may be a brief break,
allowing snow to gradually melt. Then snow returns Wednesday
evening before diminishing into snow showers Thursday morning.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued August 24 at 1:08PM AKDT until August 25 at 7:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 7 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.
